mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Home-country Companies Registry or Secretary of State

Corporate Resolution of the Foreign Shareholder Appointing the Legal Representative of the Colombian S.A.S.

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, UBOs, legal representatives, signatories, and material counterparties against OFAC SDN, UN Security Council consolidated sanctions, EU consolidated list, and Colombia's domestic restrictive lists maintained by UIAF, Procuraduría, and Contraloría. PEPs require enhanced due diligence, senior-management approval, source-of-wealth verification, and ongoing transaction monitoring. Suspicious transaction reports (ROS) must be filed through UIAF's SIROS system; documentation and screening records retained for at least 10 years.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: RUES - Registro Único Empresarial y Social (www.rue.com.co) and the territorial Cámara de Comercio portal, e.g. Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Corporate names must use Latin-script characters, preferably Spanish. Non-Spanish names or acronyms must be transliterated into phonetically recognizable Spanish form for registry acceptance. The name must be distinctive, not identical or confusingly similar to existing registered names, and must include 'S.A.S.' or 'Sociedad por Acciones Simplificada' where required.
prohibited_and_sensitive_tokens: Salud (when referring to regulated health services)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: Upon rejection, the applicant may file a recurso de reposición before the same Chamber of Commerce within 10 business days of the rejection notice, and a recurso de apelación before the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio (SIC) when available. The appeal must attach the original negative name certificate, a written explanation of distinctiveness, and, for any sensitive token, the prior ministerial or supervisory authorization. If the registry fails to resolve within the applicable statutory period, the favorable name-use presumption available under Colombian administrative law may be invoked.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permitted for a non-regulated engineering CAD/BIM outsourcing entity if the virtual office contract provides a real physical street address in Colombia capable of receiving judicial and administrative notices, along with mail-handling services. Post-office boxes alone are prohibited. The company should maintain at least basic commercial substance records because DIAN may examine perma-nent establishment and transfer-pricing substance.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: 5-10% annualized risk of unannounced physical inspection for this low-risk, non-licensed engineering services profile; the probability increases if the entity declares substantial revenue without demonstrable physical presence or local substance.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Ley 1258 de 2008 (Colombian Simplified Stock Corporation Act - S.A.S.), Articles 1, 4-5, 13, 19, 21, 26-31; supplementary rules of the Código de Comercio (Decree 410/1971), Articles 110-163; Decreto Único Reglamentario 1074 de 2015, Book II (Mercantile Registry); applicable tariff agreements of the Superintendencia de Sociedades for registration fees.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registro Mercantil - Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (e.g., Cámara de Comercio de Bogotá, Medellín or Cali), operated through the RUES (Registro Único Empresarial y Social) platform, with the DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) as the counterpart authority for tax identification.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Documento Privado de Constitución (private incorporation deed) together with the Estatutos (By-Laws), filed for registration in the Registro Mercantil through the RUES registration form; notarization is optional for S.A.S. under Law 1258/2008 Article 5.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital; minimum_capital_requirement is false. The shareholders set the authorized, subscribed and paid-in capital freely in the By-Laws. Under Law 1258/2008 Article 19, contributions must be paid within one year of subscription, with default interest in case of delay. Contributions in kind or foreign currency require an appraisal; an escrow/consignment account is mandatory only where the By-Laws so provide or for share premiums.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF [•] S.A.S. - The sole shareholder, under Law 1258 of 2008, resolves: (i) the share subscription of the authorized capital set out in Clause [•] of the By-Laws is accepted, with payment terms as provided therein; (ii) the registered office at [•], Bogotá D.C., is adopted as the statutory seat; (iii) [•] is appointed Legal Representative and [•] alternate Legal Representative, with the powers conferred by Clause [•]; and (iv) the Legal Representative is instructed to register the incorporation deed with the Cámara de Comercio, obtain the NIT from the DIAN, and complete all municipal and social security formalities.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Pre-Validation and Homonimy Certificate
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social - Registro Mercantil (RUES online portal or in-person Ventanilla Única Empresarial)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Submit the proposed company names through the RUES portal for the issuance of a Certificado de Homonimia (name availability). The Chamber verifies there is no identical or confusingly similar name. Upon approval, the reservation is valid for 30 days. The certificate of homonymy is attached to the incorporation deed.
required_dossiers: Copy of identification cards (cédulas) of the shareholders or NIT if corporate
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name is rejected, modify the name or present up to three alternatives; appeal via a written request to the Chamber's Comité de Homonimia for an administrative reconsideration.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution and Legalization of the Incorporation Deed
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Notary public (optional authentication) and Cámara de Comercio - Registro Mercantil
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the Documento Privado de Constitución in accordance with Law 1258 of 2008. All shareholders must sign the deed; to facilitate future public registration and banking, signatures and fingerprints are authenticated before a notary in the city of the registered office. The deed must expressly state the share capital, term, purpose (BIM/CAD engineering drafting services), and management structure.
required_dossiers: Notary authentication minutes (acta de reconocimiento de firma) where applicable
Valid official ID or passport of shareholders
Power of attorney if a shareholder acts through a representative
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a notary raises formal objections, redraft the affected clauses and re-sign the corrected pages; any defects identified must be cured before filing with the Chamber.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mercantile Registry Filing and Certificate of Existence
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Cámara de Comercio del domicilio social (RUES online or in-person)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File the executed deed with the RUES application and pay the registration tariff. The Chamber reviews for compliance with Law 1258 of 2008, then books the S.A.S. in the Registro Mercantil, opens the Matrícula Mercantil, and issues the official Certificado de Existencia y Representación Legal. The Pre-RUT and provisional NIT are obtained for the subsequent DIAN process.
required_dossiers: Documento Privado de Constitución (signed and authenticated)
Certificado de Homonimia issued within its validity period
Proof of payment of the registration fee (derechos de registro)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Chamber issues a Requerimiento identifying formal defects, submit the corrected documents within the stated term (typically 5 working days); should the Chamber omit registration, the company may request the Superintendencia de Sociedades to opine on the effect of the registration request.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales (DIAN) - National Tax and Customs Directorate. Main portal: www.dian.gov.co. Transactional and electronic filing platform: MUISCA (Modelo Único de Ingresos, Servicio y Control Automatizado). Electronic invoicing validation and clearance API: DIAN's Facturación Electrónica web services environment (fe.dian.gov.co).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Step 1: Incorporate the S.A.S. through a notarized deed or private document registered before the local Cámara de Comercio (Chamber of Commerce); no minimum paid-in capital is required for the Colombian S.A.S. Step 2: Appoint a legal representative who is a natural person resident in Colombia (national or foreigner with valid migration status) to act as the fiscal interlocutor with DIAN. Step 3: The legal representative (or an authorized registered gestor) completes the online pre-registration in MUISCA, providing the foreign parent/shareholder's incorporation documents, the S.A.S.'s by-laws, the local address, and the economic activity codes (ISIC/CIUU 7110 and the CIIU class corresponding to computer/engineering drafting services). Step 4: Obtain the NIT (Número de Identificación Tributaria) and the RUT (Registro Único Tributario), which must include the VAT responsible status code, the income-tax responsible status, the service-export registration flag, and any applicable industry-specific codes. Step 5: Acquire a DIAN-accredited digital signature certificate (Certificado de Firma Electrónica) and register an authorized electronic invoicing software provider to enable mandatory e-invoicing. Step 6: For outbound service payments, register the S.A.S. as an exporter of services with the foreign-exchange declaration channels of the Banco de la República through a local authorized intermediary. A foreign entity cannot obtain a standalone Colombian TIN without creating a provincial branch or a local entity; the S.A.S. itself is the taxpayer for all purposes.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation - The Colombian S.A.S. is a per se resident corporation under Article 12 of the Colombian Tax Code (E.T.). It pays national corporate income tax (Impuesto sobre la Renta) at the effective headline rate of 35% on its worldwide net income, with no consensus passthrough to shareholders. There is no territorial-source election for the S.A.S.; however, export income remains taxable on net profits (gross revenue less deductible costs and expenses) with an eligible foreign tax credit for overseas taxes borne on the same profits. Distributions to non-resident shareholders are subject to a separate dividend withholding tax or additional taxation at 10% (or higher under the applicable timing rules of the Colombian dividend stack), not a passthrough of entity results. Taxable period is the Colombian fiscal year (January 1 - December 31).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Not applicable - Colombia does not recognize a check-the-box regime or any elective entity-classification rule for S.A.S.; the S.A.S. is irrevocably treated as a corporation. The only residual election for micro/small business is the 'Régimen Simple de Tributación' (SIMPLE) under Articles 903-941 E.T., but services classified under professional engineering, architectural, and BIM consulting activities are statutorily excluded from SIMPLE, so the S.A.S. cannot elect it. There are no statutory hybrid mismatch elections in Colombia: hybrid mismatch outcomes are governed by mandatory anti-abuse disallowance rules codified under the E.T. (BEPS Action 2 alignment), and a taxpayer cannot elect out of them. The S.A.S. may elect between generating financial statements in COP or a functional foreign currency for commercial purposes, but all Colombian tax filings must be expressed in COP using the certified exchange rate at the tax-basis date. No other material tax classification election is available.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: VAT - Impuesto sobre las Ventas (IVA), governed by the Colombian Tax Code (Articles 420-494 E.T.) and Decree 1625 of 2016 (single regulatory decree).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: No de minimis turnover threshold applies to engineering/BIM service providers: an S.A.S. rendering CAD/BIM services is a legal VAT responsible person (responsable de IVA) from its first taxable transaction, regardless of revenue. A narrowly scoped exemption exists under the 'no responsables' category for minor retail goods sellers with gross annual revenues not exceeding 4,000 UVT (approximately COP 190,400,000 in 2024); professional technical services are always excluded from this exemption. Since the target scope consists of offshore engineering and drafting services, the S.A.S. must file the registration and periodic VAT returns even if all sales are zero-rated exports. Total VAT returns are filed electronically on a bimonthly or four-monthly basis depending on gross turnover (two-month periods for most S.A.S. taxpayers).
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Mandatory in full. As of 2024-2025, all VAT responsible persons must issue the Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV) using a DIAN-authorized means (own software, a DIAN-approved technology provider, or DIAN's free validation front-end). The invoice must be transmitted in real time at issuance through DIAN's Validación Previa clearance API (SOAP/JSON endpoints mutually authenticated with the taxpayer's X.509 digital certificate). DIAN replies synchronously with an acceptance/validation code before the invoice is legally delivered to the customer. Each validated invoice incorporates a CUFE (Código Único de Facturación Electrónica), a deterministic hash of the invoice data, and a mandatory QR code for digital stamping. The invoice XML must be retained and stored by the taxpayer for at least 5 years. Zero-rated export invoices must include the corresponding exportation cause code, the client's non-resident tax ID, and the DIAN service-export registration. Additionally, for cross-border service exports, the S.A.S. is required to file, when applicable, the Información Exógena (annual exogenous information return) listing export transactions and to transmit the currency-repatriation data through Banco de la República's systems.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Export of services may be invoiced at 0% IVA (zero-rated with full right to claim input VAT credits and refunds) if the cumulative conditions of Articles 481 numeral 3 and 640 E.T. and Decree 2150 of 2017 are met: (i) the seller is a person or entity domiciled in Colombia (the S.A.S. with Colombian RUT); (ii) the buyer or service recipient is a person or entity without domicile or permanent establishment in Colombia; (iii) the service is effectively used or exploited exclusively abroad; and (iv) the export is supported by the required documentary chain. For offshore BIM/CAD drafting services, DIAN accepts the contract, the electronic invoice, the technical delivery/acceptance record, and the foreign remittance certificate; the governing principle is that the beneficiary of the work and the exclusive use of the drafting output are located outside Colombia. If the Colombian entity merely acts as a subcontractor for another Colombian intermediary, zero-rating fails for lack of direct export. The zero-rated treatment is not an exemption but a 0% taxed operation; therefore, the S.A.S. may claim a refund of the VAT borne on domestic inputs (e.g., software licenses, equipment, local engineering support, rent, utilities) in the same periodic VAT return, subject to DIAN's ex-post documentary audit.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Service Export Declaration ('Declaración de Exportación de Servicios') electronically filed with DIAN through MUISCA, using the specific export-of-services form; alternatively the export must be evidenced in the RUT profile and declared in the periodic IVA return as export transactions.

Factura Electrónica de Venta (FEV) with 0% export code, CUFE hash, QR stamp, the non-resident client's tax identification, and an underlying written contract or confirmed purchase order specifying the offshore infrastructure/CAD-BIM scope and the foreign location of use.

Inward Remittance Certificate (Certificado de Reintegro de Divisas) issued by a Colombian authorized foreign-exchange intermediary (e.g., a bank) evidencing that the export proceeds were actually received in Colombia in freely convertible foreign currency within the legal deadline; a signed electronic delivery/acceptance record from the foreign client should be attached for substance substantiation.
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: DIAN applies a 5-year statute of limitations for assessing VAT differences; this period extends to 10 years in cases involving suppressed transactions or fraudulent documents. If the zero-rating or the foreign remittance requirement is not substantiated, DIAN retrospectively re-categorizes the operation as a domestic taxable service, assesses 19% VAT on the invoiced amount plus moratory interest (interés de mora) from the invoice date, and adds the 'sanción por inexactitud' under Article 647 E.T. equal to 100% of the underpaid tax (200% where the inaccuracy is caused by fraud or by invoicing through artificial structures). A VAT refund obtained on the strength of false export documentation is subject to clawback plus a 20% per-year adjusted interest charge and possible disqualification from refund procedures for future periods. Criminal exposure arises under Article 402 of the Colombian Criminal Code ('Violación de impuestos' / tax fraud), with penalties of 4 to 9 years of imprisonment, and under foreign-exchange regulations, failure to repatriate the export proceeds within 180 days triggers a Banco de la República 'sanción cambiaria' that may reach 100% of the non-repatriated amount and the reversal of the zero-rating from the date of shipment. Repeated or organized fake-export operations may additionally lead to suspension of the exporter's status in DIAN and the denial of further export invoice validation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banco de la República (Central Bank of Colombia), acting jointly with the Ministry of Finance and Public Credit (Ministerio de Hacienda y Crédito Público) and the Financial Superintendence of Colombia (Superintendencia Financiera de Colombia) for the supervision of authorized foreign-exchange intermediaries. Foreign-exchange-registration duties are administered through the Banco de la República's exchange system and the DIAN for customs-related export verification.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Colombia permits general convertibility for current-account transactions, including trade in engineering consultancy, technical services, and software-related royalties, provided the operation is channeled through an authorized local intermediary and properly declared under the Foreign Exchange Regime (Régimen Cambiario) established by Decree 1735 of 1993 and External Resolution of the Banco de la República. Capital-account operations, including foreign direct investment in an S.A.S., are legally open to non-resident investors but require registration with Banco de la República via the foreign-investment information system; withholding taxes and capital-gains rules apply on outbound profit remittance and liquidation proceeds. There are no general exchange-rationing measures for bona fide corporate transactions, but documentary proof of the underlying contract, invoicing, and tax standing is mandatory at the banking and regulatory level. For offshore engineering outsourcing companies, the practical convertibility risk is low if the treasury is routed through tier-1 supervised banks and every inbound/outbound wire is matched to a registered service export.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: Exporters of goods and services in Colombia are subject to mandatory 'canalización' (channeling) of the resulting foreign-currency receivables through the foreign-exchange market. The statutory baseline requires goods exporters to bring the collection into an authorized intermediary within six months from the shipment date and service exporters to do so within four months from the date on which the invoice accrues, unless a specific external-resolution extension applies. The rule does not mandate a fixed ratio of conversion into Colombian pesos; the exporter satisfies the channeling obligation by selling the foreign currency to an authorized intermediary or depositing it in a foreign-currency checking/savings account (cuenta de compensación) maintained with such intermediary. Compliance is evidenced through the exchange declaration form (Declaración de Cambio), with non-compliance subject to monetary fines and sanctions imposed by Banco de la República and DIAN. For offshore BIM/CAD services, the four-month channeling window is typically favorable and can be observed through monthly mobilization of client receivables into the S.A.S.'s local account.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational Account with Foreign-Currency Compensating Account
Operational Account / FX Desk Dedicated Account
Cash Management Account / Market Operations Account
USD Global Liquidity Account / Treasury Clearing Account

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Feasibility rating: MEDIUM for ancillary treasury rail, LOW for full replacement of a supervised Colombian banking account. Colombian Law 1735 of 2014 created Specialized Electronic Deposit and Payment Entities (SEDPEs), which are Fintech-supervised companies permitted to hold transaction accounts for electronic payments; however, they are not licensed as full commercial banks and are not an authorized channel for foreign-exchange declarations to Banco de la República. Offshore digital EMIs (Wise, Payoneer, or similar) are legally viable only for small-value non-operational flows, temporary liquidity parking, or vendor disbursements outside Colombia. They are constrained by weak function for Colombian payroll, tax retention, and FX compliance, and by the risk of bank account termination if large invoices are paid through an unregulated EMI instead of a local authorized intermediary. Corporate treasury should therefore use one tier-1 local account as the primary liquidity anchor and Wise or a similar EMI only as a last-mile disbursement rail for non-Colombian contractors.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: The Financial Superintendence of Colombia permits risk-based remote onboarding and video-identity verification for legal entities, but in practice tier-1 Colombian banks require a high degree of in-country substance. A foreign parent's S.A.S. must submit apostilled certificate of incorporation, internal bylaws, board resolution granting banking authority, and powers of attorney of the legal representative. Most banks accept a video interview with the ultimate beneficial owner and the S.A.S. legal representative, but several institutions request a physical appearance at the branch when the entity has no Colombian employees, no registered office other than a virtual address, or when the parent jurisdiction is a tax haven. To eliminate onboarding delay, the S.A.S. should appoint a Colombian legal representative, obtain a datáfono-free/operational address, and prepare the complete legal file in advance; remote opening should be treated as a negotiation point rather than an absolute right.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: initial capital wiring from a holding company located in a jurisdiction not aligned with the actual operating beneficiaries, causing a fragmented source-of-funds trail.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized and apostilled corporate resolution approving the equity transfer, fully attested parent bank statements, audited or management financial statements of the S.A.S., BI/UBO declaration filed with DIAN, service contracts with end clients, and an explicit narrative of the cross-border treasury chain.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: UBO or legal representative classified as a politically exposed person (PEP), particularly any connection to Colombian public-sector infrastructure licensing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PEP self-identification form, official job title and employer declaration, independent proof of income or assets, source-of-funds analysis for the capital contribution, minutes of the board meeting approving the bank account, and sanctions screening report issued by a reputable global database.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: the S.A.S. is perceived as a shell because its stated activity is remote BIM/CAD drafting without local payroll, local office, or substantive operational costs.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Detailed technical service agreements showing hourly rates, project deliverables, and reporting obligations; BIM/CAD software licences; subcontractor agreements; payroll records for Colombian engineers/designers; digital infrastructure logs; and a VAT/income-tax history filing with DIAN.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: expected banking turnover is large relative to the declared equity, with heavy one-way outbound payments to related parties abroad for subcontracting.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Transfer-pricing documentation under Colombian TP rules, functional and risk profile of the S.A.S., global service contracts, invoicing flow, GL reconciliations, cash-flow forecasts, and evidence that outbound payments correspond to invoice-backed subcontractor services.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Underwriting red flag: the account is to be fed primarily through Wise/Payoneer rather than a direct supervised bank wire, raising detectability concerns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Complete EMI transaction history, centralized treasury ledger mapping the EMI rail to each project invoice, an audit log with purpose codes, bank reference letters, and a commitment to route all FX-convertible revenues through the local authorized intermediary going forward.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Compliant inbound routing for foreign direct investment into the Colombian S.A.S. must be built on a direct SWIFT transfer from the parent company's bank to the S.A.S.'s Colombian operational account. The wire should use MT103 format with the payment message indicating 'FDI equity contribution' and referencing the underlying shareholder meeting resolution. Upon receipt, the authorized local bank (or the company's external agent) must register the operation with Banco de la República under the international investments declaration (Declaración de Cambio por Inversiones Internacionales), using the corresponding foreign-investment purpose code. For USD-denominated incoming funds, the bank will typically execute a spot sale against COP at the authorized market rate, unless the S.A.S. maintains a foreign-currency compensating account. The treasury should prepare the bank with the following documentation: certificate of incorporation and bylaws, board/shareholder resolution, legal representative identification, notarized capital contribution minutes, and the final UBO certificate. If the parent transfers through an intermediary bank, the message must be transparent and contain the beneficiary's Colombian tax ID (NIT) and account number to avoid blocking. Inbound funds should not be split into multiple wires under small amounts to avoid artificially fragmented transaction profiling; a single identified wire with full supporting documentation is more defensible under AML/KYC review.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Outbound trade disbursements for the engineering outsourcing scope should be routed predominantly through SWIFT MT103 for direct supplier payments and employee contractor remittances, and through commercial documentary letters of credit for large-value equipment acquisitions or commissioned hardware purchases. The S.A.S. should attend to the following clearing rules: (i) all foreign-currency payments require the exchange declaration (Declaración de Cambio) where the payment involves a cross-border transfer; (ii) payments for imported technology or subcontracting services must be linked to invoices and contracts that demonstrate the import of services from the income-tax point of view; (iii) outbound transfers to related parties must be supported with transfer-pricing documentation if they exceed the applicable local threshold; (iv) bank reconciliation of each SWIFT transfer should reference the underlying invoice number and the DIAN 'exportación de servicios' classification where applicable. Direct backup settlements to foreign contractors may be transmitted via the local bank's FX desk at the reference market rate, or via the S.A.S.'s foreign-currency account if the counterparty requires payment in USD or EUR. For urgent payments where the beneficiary is not in Colombia, the preferred clearing rail remains SWIFT MT103 with no intermediary complexities, and for high-volume payroll subcontractors, a centralized disbursement file with same-bank beneficiary accounts should be used to reduce transaction costs.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Non-deliverable forwards (NDFs) booked with Colombian authorized intermediaries or with international banks under the applicable foreign-exchange registration rules
Deliverable currency forwards (forwards de tasa de cambio) against USD/COP trades hedged with tier-1 local banks
Cross-currency swaps (contratos de swap de moneda) for matched tenor asset-liability management on USD-denominated receivables

Over-the-counter FX options (call/put) on USD/COP, provided the transactions are executed with supervised financial institutions and comply with Banco de la República's derivative eligibility requirements

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than 31 March each year; late renewal carries additional penalties
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late renewal triggers fines imposed by the Superintendencia de Industria y Comercio; prolonged non-renewal (typically over two years) may lead to administrative strike-off of the commercial registration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Cámara de Comercio with jurisdiction over registered office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: By 31 March each year, filed together with the annual renewal of commercial registration
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-filing prevents renewal, impedes issuance of the certificate of existence and legal representation, and may expose the company to regulatory fines regarding inaccurate public records.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate Income Tax Return (Declaración de Renta y Complementarios)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in April (or according to DIAN's published calendar), with the exact date determined by the NIT last two digits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing fine of 5% of the income tax payable, plus monthly default interest (mora) on the unpaid tax; assets may be seized if non-payment persists.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual UBO Confirmation (Registro de Beneficiarios Finales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales) – UBO portal
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually in October–November, date assigned by DIAN resolution based on NIT last two digits
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Per Article 631 of the Tax Code, fines for omission or inaccuracy may reach approximately COP 22,299,000 (about USD 5,300); repeat infringement aggravates penalties.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DIAN (Dirección de Impuestos y Aduanas Nacionales)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annually between February and May, according to the DIAN calendar and NIT digit
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Non-placement or errors attract fines under Articles 641 and 651 of the Tax Code; daily penalties may accumulate until the corrected information is submitted.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: An independent statutory auditor (Revisor Fiscal) is mandatory for a Colombian S.A.S. when, as of the immediately preceding 31 December, (i) total assets exceed 5,000 SMLMV (monthly legal minimum wages), or (ii) gross annual income exceeds 3,000 SMLMV, or (iii) the company has more than 30 shareholders.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Colombian GAAP, which adopts International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS/NIIF) as issued by the IASB; Group 2 entities apply IFRS for SMEs; Group 3 micro-entities apply a simplified regulatory framework.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Each fiscal year, the legal representative must access the DIAN Beneficiarios Finales portal and confirm or update the ultimate beneficial owners' identity, shareholding percentages, and control relationships. Any share transfer during the year must be recorded in the shareholder register and reflected in the annual UBO confirmation; changes exceeding 10% ownership require proactive recalculation and immediate notification.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (Libro de Registro de Accionistas)
Register of Directors (Libro de Actas de Juntas Directivas, if applicable)
Minute Book (Libro de Actas de Asamblea de Accionistas)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 350 – USD 1,200 per year for registered office or agent services in Bogotá, Medellín, or Cali
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 1,500 – USD 6,000 per year for an independent statutory audit (Revisor Fiscal) or certified financial statement review

corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: No general preferential corporate rate for CAD/BIM outsourcing. The only material incentives are: (i) 20% corporate income tax rate for entities operating in a Zona Franca (free trade zone) subject to pre-approval and export/investment tests; (ii) tax credit of up to 25% for qualifying research, development, and technology innovation investments; (iii) accelerated deduction for fixed-asset investments in productive projects under Articles 158-1 and 158-2 of the Colombian Tax Code; and (iv) employment-linked increases in salary deductibility for new jobs created in demographically challenged regions. The standard S.A.S. engineering drafting company is ordinarily outside these benefits unless formally qualified.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulario 110 – Declaración de Renta y Complementarios (Personas Jurídicas) filed through the DIAN electronic return system (MUISCA / DIAN website) using the taxpayer's RUT and digital signature or authorized password.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: The annual corporate income tax return for a calendar-year company is due on the date assigned by the DIAN tax calendar, determined by the last two digits of the NIT. For tax year 2024, the deadline window is generally from 9 May 2025 to 22 May 2025. No broad extension exists; late installments are subject to interest and surcharges.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Colombian tax identification number under which the S.A.S. is registered with DIAN.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: State the local NIT of the S.A.S.; a non-resident parent must use its own reference only in the CbC and related-party reporting annexes, not in this box.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Primary ISIC industry code for engineering activities and related technical consultancy.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Ensure the RUT reflects ISIC 7110 and, if BIM/structural drafting is the only activity, register the corresponding secondary CIIU code. This code drives DIAN industry-level comparability for TP benchmarking.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Total worldwide revenue recognized by the S.A.S., including offshore engineering drafting and BIM service fees, adjusted for returns and discounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Foreign-source income is taxable if it arises from services rendered in Colombia or from any sale, use, or exploitation of intangible assets that is connected to the Colombian business. Incorrectly treating offshore CAD fees as non-taxable is a common audit trigger.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 42 – Costos y deducciones asignables (Costs and deductions)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Deductible operating expenses, salaries, software subscriptions, subcontractor costs, cloud computing infrastructure, depreciation, rent, and arm's-length intercompany charges.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: All cross-border intercompany charges must be supported by written contracts, contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation, and economic substance evidence. Deductions are denied for undocumented management fees, IP royalty payments to shell entities, or invoices without electronic transmission.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 50 – Rentas exentas y no constitutivas (Exempt and non-taxable income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Income items that are legally excluded from taxable base, such as dividends received from Colombian DTA-resident companies or prescribed export benefits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Do not claim software export or BIM service exemption unless the specific activity is identified in Colombian law. Tax treaty `export` clauses do not eliminate source-country taxation on a Colombian S.A.S.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 55 – Renta líquida gravable (Taxable net income)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable income after subtracting prior-year loss offsets, exempt items, and the arm's-length baseline, before applying the 35% statutory rate.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Loss carryforwards are limited to 12 years from the loss year and may only be offset against the same Colombian company's future taxable income.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 68 – Retenciones en la fuente a título de renta (Source withholdings credit)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Creditable income tax withholdings suffered by the S.A.S. on receipts from Colombian clients, interest, or other gross payments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The S.A.S. must collect electronic withholding certificates from Colombian clients. For cross-border service payments where the contracting counterparty is the foreign parent, no Colombian withholding credit is available unless the non-resident is registered for Colombian tax.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 80 – Total impuesto a cargo (Net income tax payable)
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final tax obligation after deducting prepayments, withholdings credits, and an applicable tax credits, calculated on the taxable base at 35%.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Payment must be executed through DIAN's authorized electronic banking channels in COP. A foreign parent cannot present the payment or offset with foreign tax credits on behalf of the S.A.S.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers a sanction of 5% of the assessed income tax for each month or fraction of delay, capped at 100% of the tax, with a minimum of 10 UVT where no tax is due. Late payment applies daily interest at the rate established by the Superintendencia Financiera (often 1.5% per month). Intentional failure to file may escalate to criminal fraud penalties under the Colombian Criminal Code.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 10% for dividends paid to non-resident shareholders when the profits were already subject to the 35% Colombian corporate income tax. A 35% withholding applies to dividends distributed out of income that had not been taxed at company level, unless the taxpayer is a DTA beneficiary.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a treaty dividend relief, the non-resident shareholder must: (i) obtain a Certificate of Tax Residence (CRF) from the treaty jurisdiction; (ii) provide the CRF, a Declaration of Beneficial Ownership, and confirmation of shareholding threshold and holding period to the Colombian S.A.S. before each distribution; and (iii) have the S.A.S. submit the treaty relief request to DIAN through the electronic tax service mailbox. The S.A.S. is required to retain the documentation for at least six years and, where DIAN demands, file the special withholding returns evidencing the reduced rate. Many Colombian DTAs provide 5% on direct holdings of at least 25%.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Domestic statutory withholding is 15% for interest and 15% for IP royalties and technical services. Under most Colombian double tax treaties the rate is reduced to 10% on interest and royalties, with the exception of certain treaties that preserve a 15% rate or impose a OECD BEPS substance condition for IP payments. Payments to tax-haven intermediaries are ineligible for treaty benefits and remain at the full statutory rates.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Colombian Local File and Form 120 transfer pricing return are triggered when the S.A.S. has gross assets or gross income exceeding 100,000 UVT (COP 4,706 million for tax year 2024) and executes controlled transactions. A Master File is additionally required when the multinational group's consolidated annual gross income exceeds 500,000 UVT (COP 23,532 million for 2024). The Country-by-Country report is due for group revenue in excess of EUR 750 million equivalent. Smaller companies may nonetheless need to submit Limited or Industry Specific documentation if DIAN issues a general documentation order.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Colombia does not have a standalone Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) code analogous to offshore financial centers. However, DIAN's anti-avoidance doctrine, reinforced by Article 260-2 (general anti-abuse rule), the Limitation on Benefits clauses in Colombian DTAs, and the OECD BEPS multi-lateral instrument, requires a Colombian S.A.S. to maintain genuine employees, office or cloud infrastructure, management decisions in Colombia, and risk-bearing capability. A CAD/BIM outsourcing entity that is a mere invoice-passer with no real local engineering activity will be ignored; income will be attributed to the IT service provider in the place of performance.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Understating offshore CAD/BIM receipts, using undisclosed foreign bank accounts, or issuing false invoices to move profit outside the taxable base.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Penalty for inaccurate or fraudulent return under Article 648 of the Colombian Tax Code: 20% of the omitted tax, increased to 200% where fraud or intentional misrepresentation is proven. Interest accrues from the original due date. Criminal prosecution under Article 297 of the Criminal Code imposes imprisonment of 4 to 9 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The S.A.S. legal veil may be pierced where the return is used as a sham; statutory representative and signing directors are jointly liable for the unpaid tax and penalties. DIAN may request a travel ban and preliminary asset confiscation during criminal proceedings.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Establishing a letterbox entity in a low-tax jurisdiction (e.g., Cayman Islands, Hong Kong, or remote US state) to route engineering fees without any employees, physical or digital substance, or operational control.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: DIAN will disregard the intermediating conduit and reallocate the taxable income to the Colombian S.A.S.; the full 35% rate applies on the reallocated income plus a 200% inaccuracy penalty. The intermediary may be deemed a sham, and any activities are treated as performed by the Colombian entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors and majority shareholders who set up the conduit may be personally liable for resulting taxes. Colombian courts have held that abuse of the corporate form against the treasury triggers personal civil liability; criminal conspiracy charges are possible for deliberate tax fraud.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Failing to file Form 120 or the Local/Master File, submitting a master file without local transaction detail, or using unadjusted unrelated comparables.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Failure to provide transfer pricing documentation gives DIAN the right to make a primary adjustment based on its own benchmark; a sanction of 2% of the related-party transaction value may be imposed, up to 20,000 UVT. An incomplete or unusable Local File is equivalent to no documentation.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Officers who approve transfer pricing calculations without reasonable review can be personally liable under the negative certificate of due diligence; in serious cases, criminal liability for fraudulent falsehood in a private deed may attach.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Distributing dividends to a non-resident shareholder without applying the 10% withholding or without obtaining a DTA relief certificate before payment.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The S.A.S. is personally liable for the entire unrecovered withholding (Article 370 of the Tax Code), plus a 1% monthly fine up to 200% and late-interest charges. DIAN can deny the deduction of any related distribution expense and trigger an audit of all dividend distributions for the prior 5 years.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The legal representative who authorizes payments without withholding is jointly liable for the unpaid withholding; the veil will be lifted for fraudulent non-collection. Travel restrictions may be ordered to secure the economic rights of the Treasury.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Accepting client funds through unverified personal channels, using nominee shareholders to hide ultimate beneficial ownership, or routing payments from sanctioned/high-risk jurisdictions.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Money laundering is criminalized under Article 323 of the Penal Code, carrying imprisonment of 5 to 15 years and fines of 100 to 66,700 SVT or UVT equivalents. The Financial Information and Analysis Unit (UIAF) can freeze accounts; DIAN can order asset forfeiture.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who knowingly approve irregular cash flows become co-conspirators; provisional detention and travel bans are standard. The civil veil of the S.A.S. is disregarded, exposing directors' personal assets to restitution claims and civil damages.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Concluding intercompany contracts (especially intellectual property or management services) with a related foreign enterprise but performing no actual functions and retaining no financial risk in the S.A.S.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Under the anti-abuse rule and judicial precedent, the artificial contract is recharacterized as a capitalized dividend or hidden equity contribution; the S.A.S. loses the deduction and the foreign related enterprise is assessed with deemed Colombian-source income. Punitive interest and a 200% inaccuracy penalty follow.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign artificial contracts disregard corporate law duties of loyalty and prudence; they may be sued for the company's total tax deficiency, declared jointly liable, and a travel restraint order may be issued pending audit resolution.
